message.content:
Audit ONE brief for an autocuda run on `linalg/qr_v2` (batched square Householder QR, B200, torch 2.11). Read-only, no edits. Be skeptical and quantitative. <=220 words.

THE BRIEF (worker 0, brief-35, MACRO, parent=de0d729d the global best 2478us): A "basin change" to NVFP4. Do the n512 wide trailing (W=V^T A and the apply) as ONE BIG quant-once FP4 GEMM via torch._scaled_mm_v2 (measured 5.8x vs tf32 at 4096^3). Dodge the known thin-GEMM/O(n^3)-quant walls by quantizing A_trail ONCE per outer step (amortized: that one quantized A feeds both the W-reduction and the apply across all B=640 matrices = a large compute-bound stacked GEMM). Then ONE tf32 residual-correction (re-orthogonalization) pass for accuracy. Gates: profile-confirm FP4 GEMM is compute-bound before integrating; net-win vs tf32x3i; worst-case ill-cond + diff-guard.

CONTEXT — what's already PROVEN in this run (verify against worker logs autocuda/2026-06-22-09-10-03-qr_v2-optimize-tree-worker-*-log.csv):
- W2 brief-27/35: raw FP4 on the THIN n512 trailing = 8-25x slower; on-the-fly quant = 12x the GEMM. BUT did W2 ever test QUANT-ONCE (quantize A_trail once, reuse for both sweeps across all 640 matrices) — or only per-call/per-sweep quant? This is the brief's central claim of novelty. Grep for "quant-once", "quantize once", "reuse", "amortize".
- W0 brief-29: torch._scaled_grouped_mm has NO FP4 kernel for the batched shape (only per-matrix 2D _scaled_mm = 640 launches). DOES the brief's "one big stacked GEMM" plan actually have a working batched FP4 GEMM primitive, or does it hit the same 640-launch wall? This is the make-or-break feasibility question: can W=V^T A for 640 matrices of [512x32]^T @ [512x480] be done as ONE _scaled_mm call (e.g. reshaped/stacked), or is it inherently 640 calls?
- The n512 trailing is only ~38% SM-throughput / latency-bound (not compute-bound). FP4's throughput advantage only materializes on compute-bound GEMMs — can ANY reformulation make this batched thin-ish trailing compute-bound?

THREE QUESTIONS:
1. Is "quant-once" genuinely untested and does it plausibly change the 12x-quant verdict, or did W2 already amortize quant and still lose?
2. Is there a WORKING batched FP4 GEMM primitive for this shape, or does brief-35 die at the same 640-launch / no-grouped-FP4 wall W0 brief-29 hit? (decisive)
3. Even if FP4 GEMM works, is the n512 trailing compute-bound enough for FP4's 5.8x (a 4096^3-square number) to materialize on a B=640 batch of small/thin GEMMs — or is it latency/launch-bound so FP4 throughput is irrelevant?

End with: VERDICT: APPROVE (one-line reason) or RESCOPE (one-line reason + better target). Be decisive — given heavy FP4 dead-end history, is quant-once a real new dodge or a re-tread?
